title: The end is near.
content:
I think TEKO is finished.

I'll quickly explain the latest patch (u9.1.1) and then I'll tell you some important things.

- Improved the run save system: previously, when closing the game suddenly or exiting from the settings to the main menu, the run would save in any intermediate state no matter what, so sometimes when trying to return to the run, the game would get frozen between states. I actually shouldn't have ever put those 2 save points because the game was already saving well enough, and it was what caused the biggest issues. The run now saves correctly when the player is on the Shop Filter screen (the new feature). It no longer saves in the shop when using items even if you're not in the shop (this error has been happening since it became possible to use consumables on the play screen). You should now be able to exit to the Main Menu in the middle of chip plays (I had previously forbidden this due to bugs). According to my fixes, it only has to save when you draw chips for the first time, once per round. In the shop, it should save whenever items are used or bought.

I finally understand why many indie games take months to make a system like this. Some games even leave EA and still haven't finished their Save System. Well, in my case, it's guaranteed that it should work at least 90%. Please, if you notice specific things that don't save correctly, let me know. I promise to fix everything I'm aware of. I tested it on my own and didn't see any bugs! remember that the game gets little feedback, there are only a few of us playing TEKO.

- Now, if the player has a lot of chips, on the chip display on the play screen, the text will shrink so it fits properly.

- When entering the Codex, Preview Boss, Settings, or Pocket selector (all menu screens), previously on Discord/Steam's rich presence it appeared as if the player was in a run instead of "Main Menu". This has now been fixed.

- The tutorial screen for new players was changed to match the current aesthetics.

That's all.

Since I started creating my third game, I've come up with things for TEKO. This is great, it seems my imagination is back at its peak. I feel really good and I'd like to keep it that way. Maybe, by putting energy into another project, I've stopped feeling so much pressure with TEKO. Or maybe it's a mental effect generated because TEKO's development is finally coming to an end. Just to clarify, this doesn't mean I won't make content expansions. Finishing the technical development is one thing, and the amount of gameplay is another. TEKO aims to be infinite in that regard.

In a few months, I'll probably need testers for the 3D RPG I'm creating. So you can join the Discord. I'll announce and give important information there in the future.

I'd like to improve my first game (Almohadin). It's finished, but there are things I never polished, like the interface. And I'd also like to make a system for it to be played entirely with a keyboard or controller, because I've noticed it's easy to implement in such a simple game. Thanks to my TEKO knowledge, I'm capable of improving my first game. Maybe I'll do it at some point. I'll never close the doors on continuing to develop any of my projects. This is something I love doing. And I still love AEFTB just as much as the first day. I have a sense of attachment to every game I make. It's very likely that in a few months we might see a beautiful, huge update that will leave everyone surprised. I don't promise it 100%, but I want you to know it's in my plans to continue with all of this.

I made an important post on Patreon (it's FREE), giving some conclusions on TEKO's balance, in case you're curious and want to see some interesting data.

A few weeks ago, I was lucky enough to be able to take a vacation. It seems that made my project improve. I remember that at the beginning of the vacation, I got really stressed because I overloaded myself with tasks. I think this was inevitable. I took my time, meaning I didn't rush as much, but I still got tired. This is normal. It's something you have to go through. I don't want people to think I'm sick of the project just because I got exhausted for a few days! for as long as I can remember, I know that when I'm about to finish a long job, the exact same thing happens to me. And well, what happened to me a few weeks ago was a sign that TEKO was about to be completed. Now I feel a great sense of joy. I feel liberated. In fact, that's why the RPG idea came up, because I was able to clear my mind.

The truth is, it doesn't matter what happens anymore. I finished it. I did what I promised. TEKO is a fact, it's real. I'm satisfied now, I finished it just the way I imagined it from the beginning (even better). I don't regret anything, these 2 years of development, all the effort it took, the frustration. Today I can say I overcame it. I want that, even if only 5 people play my little game, the few who have seen it, to be witnesses of what consistency can achieve, and for it to serve as an example for their own lives; in the end, that's what all this I achieved is about: inspiring others. If I could do it, you can too. Don't give up, and even if you have obligations and boring things in life, never forget what makes you happy and truly entertains you, and never abandon your inner child. Finally, I did what I promised Pixi many years ago. If my old friend were real, he would be proud.

title: Things are changing
content:
The Artwork:

I didn't think it was that big of a deal, enough to receive several messages from different people criticizing my latest artwork. Still, being self-critical, there was room for improvement. And so, I did it.

Briefly: at first, I had a very colorful artwork with too many elements, very "rough" because the lines were ultra-thick, but with a lot of personality. Then, I changed it to an overly simple cover, with just a single character and nothing else. Both images had things that could be improved, so I combined the two: keep it simple, but at the same time incorporate something to properly fill the rest of the canvas, while representing the game's genre somehow.

Currently, the cover shows the 2 most important characters in TEKO: Pixi / Yeni. Yes, they are the ones that appear the most on the cards; then there's Talio and Gasparov. If you pay attention, you'll notice there are many sprites that relate to each other (BECAUSE THEY ARE THE SAME CHARACTER DRAWN IN A DIFFERENT WAY!). Also, I drew cards. The problem with my game: it's very complicated to represent "chips" and "cards" because they don't work like in other games. What did I do? I represented them more classically as if they were from a normal deck. And I took the opportunity to place one of the most important elements of the game (The Crystal Tower), creating a combination between Poker and Tarot cards.

In the post where I announced the new visual changes, when I said the new elements represented the game better, I was specifically referring to the new trailer and screenshots. However, the game's cover has to be simple, and it isn't always obligated to represent it faithfully. Even so, I wanted to change things, so I decided to reuse the old background (the wooden table, the purple tapestry, and the green rug) and the yellow color from the old text. And I redrew Pixi in a realistic way!

Yes, I'm so sorry, Pixi. You scare people, everyone prejudges you. You know what? Unfortunately, with the previous design, people were afraid to get into my game because he seemed like a deformed and poorly drawn creature. In my opinion, he was always cool. But I had to update him to draw more attention and make it clear that he's an ALIEN BIRD! Before, he looked like something else and people could get confused.

And no, I wasn't going to waste the illustration of Yeni. So, I put them both together. Besides, Yeni is holding an Ultracolor Chip, subtly representing one of the most important elements in TEKO.

I think this is the definitive work. Usually, when I'm very sure of something, I don't listen to others. But, when I finished the previous artwork I still had doubts. That, added to the fact that some people wrote to me (respectfully) about what they thought of my "aaaah goon waifu bait cover", made me rethink things and generate new ideas. In my opinion, things are much better now. Even so, I'll never discredit my own work. So far TEKO has had 4 covers, and I don't hate any of the 4. They're all different, and each one has an EXPLANATION and a MEANING. Until you understand this, it's impossible to know why I did things the way I did.

Anyway, I'm proud of having taken the time for this. I got a bit stressed out, not from drawing, but from coming up with new ideas and the concept I wanted to capture. Now the elements of poker + 2D fantasy should be understood.

I'm never going to underestimate people who share their opinions about my stuff. Although, art is subjective. Even so, I want you to know I always read the comments. I understand people, and I try to find a middle ground between what I want and what others want. Obviously, I'm always the priority. But if there's room for change and people want a change, if I think it's a good idea, I'll do it. I'll always be open to opinions, especially if they are made respectfully like they have been so far.

The Demo:

I want more people to wishlist my game. At the same time, I want more people to play TEKO. I'm going to prepare a new DEMO completely faithful to the latest version, which will also HAVE THE FULL GAMEPLAY LOOP and a lot of content. Yes, the pockets and cards will be limited, but it'll have so much to offer. And this will lead to a lot of people getting interested in the full version. Until now I was holding back, because I wanted to improve the official version. Soon, when I finish polishing the game 100%, I'll launch the demo, and this will help a lot. I'm excited and really looking forward to it.

My next game:

I'm making an RPG. Yes. I don't know what's going to happen, I'm not promising anything. I just want to show you a bit of what I'm doing. I'm taking my time, trying to enjoy and think things through, imagining what my ideal game for this subgenre would look like. I have a lot of plans and you'll see more stuff (plus I created a YouTube series to document everything from scratch). I hope this new path turns out great. This isn't going to replace any of my other simultaneous projects, just clarifying just in case, I'm doing it in my free time. TEKO's development is not affected by the RPG.

NEW! Shop Filter Feature. Now, after beating the round 13 boss, the player will be able to choose which items they don't want to show up on sale in the shop for the rest of the run. This feature has also been added as an achievement.

Along with the Shop Filter, you can also revert the pre-bans made to cards!

Both in the Shop Filter and the Codex, the 'Current' text for the cards values should now be visible. I think this wasn't happening before; it has been fixed. There was a small issue calling the respective lines.

Added a new button to reset the card ban selection in the codex.

2 Steam achievements (pre-ban & boss preview features) have been fixed and can now be earned retroactively.

Fixed two errors when changing profiles: (1) a white border would appear on the sides of the screen, it was a screen manager bug. (2) On the next run, shapeless chips would appear instead of the normal ones.

Now mod texts can stack in the tooltip (if you have more than 1 mod of the same type, it will show, for example, 'x2' instead of repeating the name and its description twice).

The text on the button to buy card slots has been made smaller (in its Spanish version, it didn't fit well before).

title: Good news for TEKO
content:
I'm happy to announce that I've finally revamped some elements of the Steam Store Page for TEKO. I've wanted to do this for a long time, and I finally managed to do it. I changed everything, from the trailer to the cover image and the description. Now everything looks prettier and better represents the game in its current state.

I have a lot of plans for the game. I'll make some of them a reality, others will depend on the motivation people give me. If I see that more and more people like the game, I plan to put in more effort. During all these years of development, I NEVER relied on feedback or public approval, but now more than ever, I think making extreme new changes will only be worth it if I get a larger player base.

Some of the changes I have in mind for upcoming versions are:

  • Control: I'd like the game to support any kind of input. Currently, you can only play with a mouse, but in the future, I'd like it to be 100% playable with: just a keyboard, PlayStation/Xbox controllers, Steam Deck, etc.

  • Translation: I'll be completely honest, I don't have money, much less to pay for localizations. My plan is the following: find people who want to collaborate for free on localization, then run all the game's text through an automatic translator, and have the volunteers just fix the mistakes instead of doing every single line one by one; I'd just need quality and coherence control. This is the best way for me to do things. But I absolutely need native speakers for each language. I'm not going to rely solely on a machine to translate everything; I mandatorily want at least one person to manually review each language. If at any point someone is interested in helping me out for free, you can let me know, and we can implement a new translation. We already have the English and Spanish text complete, now I want to expand specifically to ALL LANGUAGES, no matter which one.

  • Shop item ban mechanic: this is similar to the pre-ban system, but instead of before the run, it's during it. And it'll only affect items on sale, not other elements like packs. It will serve to block items from showing up when you reroll. It'll be incredibly important for the game's balance.

  • Balance: I have some things planned for balance, like changing the rarity of cards, or customizing the difficulty more for each Pocket.

  • Content: I want to add extreme mechanics that change the whole game, especially with Pockets. I have too many good ideas, and when I say too many I mean that implementing all this content would mean expanding TEKO's gameplay by more than 1000 extra hours. It is, without exaggerating, insane. Not just the pocket ideas (the game's core mechanic), but cards too. I can start working on this whenever I want, since everything is written down and planned, but I can't jump into the void and start a new streak of new content without the backing of a solid community. Therefore, I prefer to take a break from development to focus my efforts on increasing the amount of people playing TEKO, so I can take big steps later. I'M WILLING TO SUPPORT THE GAME FOR MONTHS OR YEARS. Never doubt that.

I just added 2 new achievements to Steam (the 2 new unlocked mechanics, added in version 9.0).

I just updated the whole website, especially the Wiki, I recommend you go in and see what's there, plus I improved the tierlist. I had a lot of fun doing this.

Don't forget to join the Discord server, you can ask me any questions or give any kind of feedback or idea.

Don't forget that you can support me on Patreon. I'll soon upload some surprise content there, even some FREE POSTS! (yes, you can follow me for free).

Please, consider leaving a Review on TEKO's Store Page, it would help me a lot. The game's visibility truly depends on this.

- The logic implemented in the previous patch (the perk sprite not showing up as hovered when entering the shop) has been replicated for all shop rounds, not just the first one.

- Improved the size of the Pocket Visualizer; chips now look bigger and only look small when there are more than 60.

- An extra value no longer appears when buying chips. Previously, where the pocket is drawn, if we had 40 chips and bought one, it would momentarily show "42" instead of "41".

- Now, every time a consumable is used, it will always play a sound effect.

- Special combos (TRIXI, etc.) will play a sound effect when triggered.

- Fixed the logic that caused the game to crash when finishing the tutorial as a new player. And also fixed the settings logic when entering TEKO for the first time. I didn't know this was happening, these cases are too specific and I don't have control/vision over everything. I usually spend my time testing the things I consider most essential and critical that can cause the most problems, and since I never doubt certain things, sometimes issues happen and persist over time, and since they're never reported, I don't notice them. This error was reported by someone on the Discord server, otherwise I never would've found it. I want you to make an effort to join the Discord and report if you find a serious issue like this. I know it's exhausting to take a few minutes to report things, but feedback is necessary for the game to be 101% polished, and I'm dependent on the players in that regard. Anyway, as months go by I end up doing everything myself; but I want you to keep in mind that I ALWAYS read all the feedback and if there's an error, I try to fix it no matter what. That's what I'm here for, I'm very active and constantly on the lookout for anything that can improve the experience, I really like what I do, I love developing, so I take it very seriously!

- Optimized the delta time system. I previously implemented something that modified the timings and it ruined the experience for some people with low FPS, so I reverted it. I didn't know this was working poorly, because I always tested the game at 165 fps.

- Optimized the particles of color tubes. Previously, if the player was playing at 60 fps or lower, the particles fell as if they were frozen.

- Optimized buttons; some of them would move slowly on low FPS.

- Removed the option to choose FPS in the settings. At least for now, I think it's the best approach, since it's not a very useful option and it has caused some issues.

- The yellow outline on cards is now displayed correctly (it used to render below the shadow) on selection screens like Masquerade or Dice (consumables).

- Changed the shadow and positioning of the Base X Multi sprites to make it more consistent. I also improved the jump animation when gaining value; the multi and base used to have different animations, but now they're the same.

- The price of mods is now rendered on top of all mods when you have more than 3 (Oracle Card) and they are very close together in the shop.

- Mikello Card and Manolo Boss should now trigger the chip deletion sound effect when one is removed.

- Duplicating a chip with Printer no longer triggers the draw animation.

- Supposedly, it was possible to equip mods on Sinister Cards. I added a check to prevent this. I hope it works properly now.

- The Binocular consumable screen should now correctly show the current values of the cards to choose from.

I feel kind of weird, confused, and dissociated.

I've made quite a few changes and fixes, aiming to leave Early Access. I'll leave the commit log here, but unordered, and without differentiating whether they were modifications to the beta or the live version... because I don't even remember.

To give you an idea of how lost I am: a few days ago I spent hours trying to figure out why the Orange Tube wasn't working, but in the end, it was because I was playing with the Hacker Pocket (-1 draw XD).

Anyway, here are the patch notes:

- Improved the buying animation for all items in the shop.

- Improved the discard/draw animation (more fluid). Also, shadows now appear behind the chips when they travel from the pocket to the hand or from the hand to the pocket.

- Improved the discard animation at the end of the round (upon winning it).

- Fixed a bug that made it impossible to turn the starting card into a Sinister when starting a run with Chosen/Warlock Pockets. Instead of working properly, the card was deleted.

- Optimized and fixed a memory leak when hovering over certain buttons and when rendering stickers. I also improved some logic to make the game consume fewer processing resources.

- New shader that slightly improves the saturation/contrast of the whole game. It's very subtle but it looks great.

- Fixed The Beast Card. It wasn't working at all before.

- Improved screen animation fluidity after winning rounds.

- The numberless trait is now rendered correctly when doing draw/discard.

- The Codex screen no longer breaks after finishing a run with Chosen Pocket.

- Now, chips with a Stagnant Sticker that stay in the hand when making a play will trigger an animation when adding base multiplication.

- Improved the height consistency of floating texts when certain steps are executed (for example, the red text for the special combo used to appear higher up; now everything is at the same Y-axis point).

- Fixed the outglow of mods and the blender on the selection screen.

- Now, every time you gain money, the money counter should play a scale-up animation, and a scale-down animation when you lose it.

- All miniature chips (the representation of selected chips above the hand) should now play a short spawn and travel animation from the right instead of doing it in a random and erratic way.

- The logic that made some relics play animations when entering the shop had disappeared; this has now been fixed.

- Flowar Card now executes properly.

- There shouldn't be any more resize issues in windowed mode.

- If the chip only has Extra Base, the tooltip and its text won't look as small in the miniatures section.

- The hovered sprite of shop perks will no longer appear right after finishing a round; it was an annoying visual thing.

- Aligned some elements on the memories screen for better aesthetic consistency.

- Chips that get destroyed for having Mikello Card will now play the same disintegration effect as in other cases.

- Miniature chips shouldn't disappear when using the Green Tube.

- Fixed a visual bug that caused the frames of relics underneath the top relic to show when dragging and dropping it.

That's all. I really want to rest. I'm mentally exhausted. Sorry. Lately, I don't have many reasons to push myself so hard on the game, and yet I still do it, as seriously and dedicatedly as I can. Even though I haven't sold more than 10 copies in the last 2 months, it seems my willpower is stronger than anything.

I have HUNDREDS of content ideas, but since my mental health has deteriorated and I literally make nothing doing this, I'll have to rest more than usual. I want to push through to leave EA, but I don't want that to be the end of TEKO. Anyway, it's already a very complete game and can be fully enjoyed right now.

I feel really bad. In a few days, I'll be seeing professionals, getting rediagnosed first, and then I'll see how to proceed. I just wanted to let you know I'm not having my best moments right now. Despite the emotional instability, as you can see, I'm working hard. But I think that's the cause of my problems: being obsessed with finishing this game.

So, without a doubt, please know that I'm already finishing this up, at least the first big finished version. As I said before, I promise to keep up with monthly content expansions if there are people willing to help me test, and if there's a minimum audience interested in completing the game.

• Clarified the description of one of Outlaw Pocket's mechanics.

  • Now when there are more than 12 cards, they should render better (they used to have a weird flickering effect).

  • Added an anti-crash check for certain situations where winning a round caused an unexpected error.

  • Kimi Card should now work properly when starting a run with it (Warlock/Chosen Pocket).

  • Tooltips of 'miniature' chips will now be wider and have a smaller font so they don't go past the top edge of the screen.

  • Reverse Blender should now be usable correctly even if there's only 1 relic slot available. It should've always done that, but it seems it was miscounting the slot amount before.

  • Bosses that take away your money can now reduce it down to -$10 (there were no limits before).

  • When finishing a run with Chosen Pocket, entering the Codex caused a bug. This has been fixed.

  • Fixed a bug that prevented selling Stamp Block outside the shop.

  • Fixed an exploit that allowed having infinite copies of cards using the Drop Mod. This wasn't intended. If you find any illogical replicable mechanics that give you a clear advantage and seem outside the game's design, please report them!

  • Sinister Cards can't be rerolled anymore. If you find another way to reroll them, let me know and I'll fix it. It wasn't a feature.

  • Fixed spacing issues for relic mods in the memories tooltips.

  • When dragging Cards, tooltips from other on-screen elements won't show up anymore if your cursor hovers over them.

title: 9.0! The BIGGEST update ever.
content:
ULTRA UPDATE - u9.0.0!
I've been working on this update for months, knowing that the game still looked bad and needed to be polished to the max so the gaming experience would be the right one. I know my weakness was the visuals, so that's what I worked on the most: IN TOTAL I MADE OVER 200 CHANGES. Aside from the aesthetics, I used the momentum to create new features and make the game easier for everyone, with a lot of QoL and other useful resources.

Here's a summary of everything I did:
VISUAL/SOUND
- Total overhaul to the OST. All the music was improved and extended for a better experience.
- Total overhaul to the sound effects. Now all elements and actions have sounds. All buttons make a sound when clicking/releasing.
- Total rework to the Cards: they look much better: now they're bigger, their borders are more colorful and have defined black lines on the outside, they have more space for the elements inside, they no longer have subpixel issues, therefore the interpolation is correct and the images fit perfectly inside the borders, plus I improved their quality. I also improved the drag animation, when they move they tilt to the side, plus they arrange themselves better when there are a lot of them. I also reworked the way Sinister Cards look.
- Added a shadow in the bottom left corner to exactly all elements in the game. Some elements get bigger when hovering over them, and their shadow behind gets bigger to achieve a zoom-in effect.
- All usable items will do a color pulsating effect when clicked. Other interactable elements will also do something similar.
- Added an erratic floating effect to most interactable elements.
- Improved all buttons in all interfaces throughout the game. Now they have better coloring, they all have a sinking effect when clicked, and activate after releasing the click. Plus, they no longer have an ugly outline effect, instead they darken when hovered. Some buttons have been made smaller, especially those in the main menu.
- All texts have a more defined black stroke, the overall quality and definition of the entire game increased.
- Movement animation speeds have been accelerated for all elements in the game (for example, when you buy an item and it travels to your inventory).
- New animation for items when selling them, they disappear and for a second a "$" sign appears. Plus, the money display now does a jumping effect every time this happens.
- Adjusted the positioning of all elements on the game screen, the shop, and the main menu. Now there's more space, everything is better organized, and besides, no element touches the edges of the screen.
- Rework to all item screens (for example, the packs where you get something), they all have the same visual coherence and all their elements were improved to match the rest of the game.
- Images that have changed: inventory sprites for packs/stickers and mods, now they're a sort of table made of colorful precious stones; the Codex; the Card slots; Hacker Pocket; Manual; Number-only Stickers; Locker; Pillbox; the cancel/confirm buttons (now they're an 'X' and a green checkmark); Pirinola.
- Images I've deleted: the one behind the money amount; the wooden table located behind the Cards; the green carpet behind the Chips.
- Card sprite reworks: Last Man Standing, White Spark Legend, Fair Trade, La Yeni, Cheers, Betrayal, Idle Overlord, Transgressor, Filling.
- Fixed items that had imperfect borders, for example, Consumables had white subpixels and that made them look pretty ugly.
- Now Chips will float when selected, they look much better, they move in a more fluid way.
- Improved the descriptions of dozens of items that had inconsistencies between them, for example, Cards that gave x multi, before it said "+x" instead of "x". Now it's neater.
- Improved Mod coloring. Their display inside Cards has also improved.
- Now the perk reward screen when beating a boss looks much better, it has colors and the description. I also improved its tooltip and the image that represents it.
- Added the missing Stickers and all Chip types to the Codex.
- Now the selected combo display is split into 3 and moves so it's not so static. In my opinion, it turned out beautiful.
- Entire visual rework to the color tubes, now they actually look like tubes.
- Rework to the draw/discard animation. Now it looks like Chips come out of the Pockets, they appear from below and then disappear.
- Fixed inconsistency in Chip colors, now everywhere it's ordered like this: cyan, pink, green, orange.
- I completely changed the background's color palette, and I also darkened the sprite so it's not as distracting. It's much more subtle, but it changes colors faster.
- Text no longer overflows inside any button or screen.
- Rework to all Stickers so they don't lose quality. Before, being such small elements, they looked a bit bad. Now I changed them to vectorized files and they look perfect.
- Added round record stat for every difficulty of every Pocket in the main menu.
- The base and multi displays now jump every time value is added to them.
- Reworked the screen that appears after winning a round.
- New animation when deleting Chips and Cards. They do a sort of fading into ashes (they break into tiny pieces).
- The speed of the scoring stage (from when you hit 'PLAY' until the score goal is reduced) improved significantly, but in a more gradual and much more measured way. And if there are a lot of scoring elements, the time will conveniently shorten so you don't waste so much time waiting. It's much more responsive.
- More coherent animations for Cards that trigger when entering the shop (for example, those that delete other Cards, like The Beast). Now, before the Cards rearrange themselves, they stay still, giving time for the Cards to do their animations, and when they all finish acting, they rearrange normally.

QOL/BALANCE
- Added 3 new buttons for better Mod management: (1) auto-equip all (2) auto-unequip all (3) unequip Mods from specific Cards. It's no longer necessary to do it one by one.
- NEW Ban System: now you can choose which Cards you don't want to appear in your run.
- Now all Consumables can be used on the game screen. This is one of the biggest balance changes because it will allow for new strategies, for example, modifying the chips on the spot.
- Now it's possible to get Cards and have them take effect immediately, for example, those that give stats like mana.
- Now it's possible to preview the bosses you're going to fight against. This helps decide a better strategy.
- Added 2 utilities for the Chip miniatures (when selecting Chips from your hand, they are drawn at the top over a glass table): now when hovering over them they show their corresponding tooltips, and you can also CHANGE THEIR ORDER! now it'll be easier to interact with Chips that have special effects.
- Now it's possible to replace a Card if you open a Card pack and all slots are already full. This allows you to pivot to other builds more easily.
- Expanded the scoring limits, now strings beyond a decillion are written in scientific notation. It's possible to go further.
- Infinity system: it's possible to reach infinity. Upon reaching this, it will only be possible to score infinity to reduce the score goal.
- I reduced the Score Goal and the overkill penalty when playing with the Forbidden Pocket.
- You can access the posts of the latest updates by clicking on the version number in the Main Menu (top right corner).
- Added a button to choose a random Pocket and difficulty.
- Added a button to see all Pockets at once (like the codex) to visualize them more easily and choose which one to play with greater clarity.
- Added an indicator next to the Pocket to know how many available shuffles are left during the round.
- With the Empanadino Card it will be possible to skip the empanada race (this saves a lot of time).
- Flowor Boss warns in its tooltip that it disables action Mods (thumb/iron/bat/ball).
- Removed Cam Mode (it moved the elements to allow content creators to place their webcam more easily). There's no screen space for this currently!
- Added clarification to the Castle Consumable (which level it upgrades).
- Warlock Pocket no longer gives locked Cards.
- Now the score goal percentage will also increase depending on: the amount of Action Cards; the money saved; the amount of Pro Mods. PS: not in every round!
- Clarified that the Sinister Trait cannot be duplicated.
- Changed the Linen Pocket description so it's easier to understand what it does.
- Cheapskate Card should make the reroll price $0 at any time regardless of when it's obtained. Sale Card will do the same (always lowering the price).
- Extra Mods indicator in the inventory text. It's possible to have more than the Mod limit, for example, when a Card that had equipped Mods is destroyed. Now it will show, for example, "12+2" and they will be added to the queue. When spaces are freed up, the queued Mods will appear.
- I added a button to sort the Pocket's Chips by color, number, or shape, in the visualizer for all the Chips the player has.
- Now the page and section where the player left the Codex before exiting are saved.
- Added a table in the Pirinola tooltip, and a new description, that precisely shows all the data you need to know.
- Overkill was limited to 999.999% to avoid string issues (good luck reaching that number XD).
- No more than one Lankvian Boss will appear on the highest difficulty. Previously, this increased the score goal too much if it repeated.
- Bosses can no longer repeat consecutively when there's a double boss.
- Now it will be possible to exit by right-clicking on these screens: manual, pocket visualizer, pocket selector, codex, settings, boss preview, memories.
- Now it's possible to delete Memories. You can also see more expanded info to visualize all the Cards from the run.
- Improved the notification box's functionality. When Cards upgrade Cards, each one will be put in the queue unless they are Cards like Tryhard, which upgrade the same combo, in that case it will show, for example "Tryhard x2" if there are 2 Cards.
- Added max draw, shuffles, minimum chips, starting money to the Pocket tooltip.
- Manual rework: now it offers information about special combos.
- Abandoning a run will now add stats and unlock things as if it were a defeat.
- Now, at the end of each run, memories appear as a form of summary.

BUGS
- Optimization, I removed hundreds of unnecessary lines of code one by one that served to constantly check things. Deleted a ton of redundant and repetitive stuff. Refactored and unified several scripts.
- Now Memories (run history) take up almost no space. I did a total rework to data saving.
- When Alchemy Card triggers, there won't be visual inconsistencies in some elements anymore.
- Some effects, like for example, the Draw amount, should now work properly when continuing a run.
- Fixed an interaction that allowed selecting 2 item types at once (for example, Cards and Consumables).
- Fixed a crash when rerolling and hitting the rare Card pity.
- When changing/deleting a profile, the game will restart (a loading screen will appear) to properly execute the changes.
- Quitting the game in the middle of a play shouldn't break the run.
- The Hourglass Sticker can no longer delete Chips beyond the minimum limit.
- If a Boomerang Chip is discarded, it won't return to your hand.
- Now the Magic Pocket increases the Pillbox's efficiency correctly.
- Fixed Dopamine and Start from scratch tooltips. If the player had negative money, negative values appeared.
- Straight 3 is better than two pair in numbers. Before it was the other way around, and it brought scoring issues.
- Now beating the final boss will give a perk if you continue in endless mode.
- The music pitches down at the beginning of the turn where you have 1 mana instead of in the middle of the previous play.
- Using Pentagram (to turn a Card into Sinister) correctly removes the equipped Mods from the converted Card.
- Even if you have negative money, you can reroll the shop if the roll is $0.
- Fixed all bugs generated by Chips that had numberless Stickers. They previewed incorrectly, interacted poorly with combos, and now they sort correctly in your hand.
- Now all screens transition correctly. Before, some elements lingered for a few frames when switching screens.
- Dragging a Card won't accidentally select its Mod if the cursor happens to land on that position.
- Texts no longer break when exiting and returning to a game.
- Fixed a Transfuser Consumable bug that wouldn't let you select Chips correctly.
- Fixed several bugs on the Mask/Masquerade/Ticket screen.
- Fixed several descriptions in the Memories tooltips that didn't show Card values.
- The engine was updated after 2 years of not touching it. I've switched to the most stable version. This should achieve a subtle difference in performance.
- Item purchasing is no longer blocked while buying Consumables.
- Cards no longer overflow on the blender screen when there are many.
- When having a lot of points, the manual no longer calculates infinitely to show base x multi (this caused the screen to lag).
- Fixed the bug that showed some Pro Mods could be equipped on Cards where it actually wasn't allowed.

Thanks to everyone who believed in me. We're very close to leaving Early Access. TEKO already has a lot of content, but I'm going to make a huge expansion for version u10.0. Besides, I have to make several balance changes.

Remember that I barely have resources, I'm completely alone and plus I almost have no feedback. This path was very hard for me. Even so, I haven't given up and now it shows that this is a serious game.

Honestly, to this day I think I do deserve to do well and for the game to be more recognized. Only now I can say it, before I didn't think I deserved such a thing. But I've been working over 4,000 hours on this project. I really deserve good things to happen to me.

We're just one step away from finishing. The game is completely playable and enjoyable in its current state. Thanks for your patience. I'm sorry for rushing in the past, I shouldn't have released the game in such a raw state. It won't happen again with my next games.

This isn't over, it's just the beginning.

PS: obviously I'm open to any suggestion, bug reports, balance feedback, etc. I ALWAYS WILL BE. I actively listen to the community. Never forget: I'm here to offer you the best experience possible. My dream is to make a living out of this!

Here's a video that summarizes all the changes the game had during this year of development:

title: TEKO u9.0.0 BETA!
content:
Finally. The new version is here!
I'm almost done with all the new systems and features, along with the biggest aesthetic overhaul in TEKO's entire history.
To try out this version, you'll have to go through your Steam library:
Settings > Game versions & Betas > Private versions (Check Code).
tekobeta1234

Select the beta version, the game will update, and you'll be ready to play the new version.

There will be tentative changes, things that aren't 100% finished yet, but overall it's already working pretty well. There might be crashes, bugs, exploits... so please, report all issues on Discord! I enter every day and check all the reports.

I recommend backing up your data at C:/Users/-/AppData/Local/TEKO.

I need testers. This version is focused on QoL and aesthetics, and making sure everything runs smoothly without bugs. There are so many changes! I've been working on this update for over 2 months. Later I'll make a detailed report with every change made, but for now I'll leave you with the surprise until you hop in.

The plan is that, after finishing 9.0, I can resume my normal activity by making a version 10.0 with tons of new content. So I hope everything goes well.

The only way to go back from the beta to the original version is by deleting your cloud data and Memories history, so I really don't recommend going backward (anyway, this new 9.0 beta version is much better than the live 8.0, so there's no point in going back), but I'm letting you know just in case someone wants to play both versions at the same time: due to the structural change between the two, it's hard to keep the data. If you go back from 9.0 to 8.0 without deleting your Memories, there will be a crash because the old version can't read the new strings.
